name: Calendar Preview
description:
Replaces the date menu's single-day event list with the next N appointments, regardless of day boundaries.

GNOME's calendar popup always shows exactly one day — by default today, which is of little use for planning. This extension puts a rolling list of the next appointments in the same place, drawn from the same Evolution Data Server calendars the shell already uses and updated live through org.gnome.Shell.CalendarServer.

• Number of appointments configurable (default: 6)
• All-day entries included by default, and shown as such
• Running appointments are marked
• While you browse another day in the month grid, the native day list takes over again
• Clicking the list opens GNOME Calendar

The lookahead window widens automatically when needed, so the list stays filled across quiet periods.

Note: the shell's calendar time range is global state shared with the month grid. The extension re-asserts its window whenever the date menu opens.
